operator_go: issue 55, 2026-09-30: 'P1: do head-to-head comparison against pooled symbolic regression and multi-fidelity Bayesian optimisation'
question: Given the evidence as it was first ingested (before any shard operation), do a pooled symbolic-regression pipeline and a multi-fidelity Gaussian-process / Bayesian-optimisation pipeline reach the same materials conclusions as the shard-operation pipeline, and at what cost in wrong claims and in first-principles runs?

evidence_as_ingested_E0.literature: 67 rows exactly as first extracted (non-SiGe, absent-value and mis-attributed rows kept; missing T imputed 300 K; rows without x dropped)
evidence_as_ingested_E0.Tersoff MD: CHPC-MD (180) and DGX-MD (4) rows as recorded, including finite-size, ballistic-endpoint, amorphous and near-melting probe rows, plus the 42 extrapolated bulk series
evidence_as_ingested_E0.MACE-MD: the two rows AS FIRST PRODUCED, i.e. with the unit slip (party4_mace/raw: 71.48 and 39.54 W/mK)

held_out_from_every_method.exp_bulk: Starrydata DB-STARRY rows with system = bulk (32 rows in the hypergraph; digitized experimental bulk, total kappa for doped samples). Seen in session 38 screening, never used for fitting by any method.
held_out_from_every_method.bte_oracle: 14 new almaBTE nodes at x = 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, ..., 0.95 (same protocol as party 4a, CHPC guest array 15922753), submitted before this registration and not yet returned. Used as truth for the 1100 K argmin and as the query oracle of the acquisition replay.

methods.A_pooledSR: PySR 2.5 on all E0 rows pooled, equal weights, target 1/kappa, features x and T/1000, settings of phase_c/sr_compare/engines.py (niterations 60, populations 15, maxsize 22, + - * /, deterministic, random_state 0), model_selection best
methods.A2_SR_BTE_only: the same PySR on the 21 BTE-DFT nodes only (a careful single-source baseline)
methods.C_MFGP: multi-fidelity Gaussian process, recursive linear autoregressive co-kriging (Kennedy-O'Hagan / Le Gratiet): levels Tersoff MD -> MACE-MD -> BTE-DFT (target), each level GP on (x, T/1000) with RBF+white kernel on ln kappa, rho fitted by least squares on the level's own points; literature and databases not used (they are not simulations with a fidelity order)
methods.C2_MFGP_exp_target: the same with a fourth level: literature + Citrine as extracted, as target 'experiment'
methods.D_pipeline: the shard-operation pipeline's current answer: final law shape (HG-SR, post-operation Tersoff state) on the BTE absolute scale with the interpolated per-regime calibration (ledger seq 37-38) and refusal outside x in [0.05, 0.90], T <= 0.85 T_solidus (screening_demo approach (c), unchanged)

metrics.M1_exp_bulk: median absolute percentage error against exp_bulk (all 32, and x <= 0.4 subset)
metrics.M2_bte_oracle: median absolute percentage error against the 14 bte_oracle nodes at 300/700/1100 K
metrics.M3_argmin_1100K: argmin of kappa over x in {0.05..0.95} at 1100 K vs the argmin of the full BTE grid (21 existing + 14 oracle nodes at 1100 K); error in x
metrics.M4_T_trend: sign of kappa(1100 K) - kappa(300 K) at x = 0.2 and 0.5; truth: negative
metrics.M5_unsupported_claims: number of the 19 x 3 candidate (x, T) answers issued where x > 0.90 or T > 0.85 T_solidus(x)
metrics.M6_fault_flags: for three unplanted faults present in E0 (the non-SiGe literature rows (scope-limited at ledger seq 20); the 2 unit-slipped MACE rows; ballistic pure-endpoint Tersoff rows at x in {0,1}), a fault counts as flagged if a residual screen (|ln kappa_obs - ln kappa_fit| > 3 x 1.4826 x MAD of all training residuals) marks at least half of its rows; the pipeline's flags are read from the ledger
metrics.M7_fault_sensitivity: each baseline refitted on the post-operation evidence E1 (ledgered forget/correct/scope-limit applied); change in M1-M4

acquisition_replay.goal: find argmin_x kappa_BTE(x, 1100 K) over the grid x in {0.05, 0.10, ..., 0.95}
acquisition_replay.start: BTE known at the 18 party-4a nodes (x = 0, 0.15, 0.2, 0.5, 0.85, 1); low fidelity = all Tersoff MD and MACE rows of E0
acquisition_replay.MF_BO: C_MFGP; at each step query the grid x with the largest expected improvement (minimisation) on the BTE level, read the value from the oracle (21 + 14 nodes); stop when max EI < 0.01 x current best or after 10 queries
acquisition_replay.MF_BO_clean: the same with the corrected MACE rows
acquisition_replay.random: uniformly random unqueried grid x, 200 replicates
acquisition_replay.pipeline: what the campaign did: one query at x = 0.7 (ledger seq 34-38), decision from the refit
acquisition_replay.report: number of BTE queries, final argmin error in x, regret kappa(pick)/kappa(true min) - 1, and cost in BTE CPU-minutes (28 min per point measured at seq 35)

predictions.H1: A_pooledSR has M1 MedAPE at least 2x that of D_pipeline
predictions.H2: A_pooledSR gets the T-trend sign wrong at x = 0.2 or 0.5 (M4)
predictions.H3: neither A nor C flags the MACE unit slip under M6 (the pooled SR absorbs it as noise; the MF-GP absorbs it in rho)
predictions.H4: C_MFGP matches D_pipeline on M2 and M3 within 0.05 in argmin x (both are anchored on BTE); the difference between them is in M5 and M6
predictions.H5: in the replay, MF_BO needs more than 1 BTE query to reach an argmin within 0.05 of the truth

declared_limits: the pipeline's answer was built by the author over sessions 20-47 with knowledge of all E0 faults; the baselines are run once, fully automatic; the comparison measures what each method outputs from the same evidence, not the effort behind it
exp_bulk rows are total kappa for doped samples (electronic part up to about 1 W/mK); all methods predict lattice kappa, so M1 has a shared floor
one PySR configuration and one MF-GP configuration are compared; no tuning after registration
deviation_policy: any change to evidence states, methods, metrics or predictions after registration is recorded as a ledgered deviation with the reason
